pattern_name: system-initiated output with no user request
short_summary: Output is emitted without a user request immediately preceding it.
ui_ux_rationale: Defines proactive system initiative and the experience of unsolicited assistance.
definition: Output is emitted without a user request immediately preceding it. The trigger is a timer, a change in sensed or task state, or the system's own decision that intervention is warranted, and the user takes no action to summon what appears.
structural_signature: An output-producing edge in the control graph whose predecessor is not a user event: a clock, a state-change condition, or an internal decision step. There is no request object attributable to the user for that output, and the interface offers no control the user could have withheld to prevent it appearing at that moment.

pattern_name: output synchronized to the live activity as it happens
short_summary: The system emits its output in step with an activity that is unfolding independently — a conversation, a performance, a learning session, a walk through an environment — so that each output appears at the moment its referent occurs.
ui_ux_rationale: Defines real-time coordination between assistance and an unfolding activity.
definition: The system emits its output in step with an activity that is unfolding independently — a conversation, a performance, a learning session, a walk through an environment — so that each output appears at the moment its referent occurs. Timing is part of the design, not an implementation detail: an output delivered late would be the wrong output. The pattern is about when material is shown, not what it contains.
structural_signature: An input stream is consumed continuously and each produced item is scheduled against a timestamp in that stream; the pipeline is held to a latency budget so that the item is presented while its referent is still current. There is no batch boundary between the activity and the output — the activity does not have to end for output to appear.

pattern_name: live-updating panel co-located with the working surface
short_summary: A persistent region sits beside the surface the user is working on and shows generated content derived from that surface's current state.
ui_ux_rationale: Defines a persistent interface region that refreshes beside the artifact.
definition: A persistent region sits beside the surface the user is working on and shows generated content derived from that surface's current state. It refreshes on its own as the work changes rather than when the user asks. The panel is not the artifact under construction; it is a running commentary on it.
structural_signature: Two co-present regions with an asymmetric dependency: region A holds the user-authored state, region B renders a derived generation, and B is recomputed as a side effect of changes to A with no invocation step. B is typically read-only or non-committal — its content does not enter the artifact unless the user acts. The adjacency is spatial (margin, sidebar, docked panel) so that A and B are read together.

pattern_name: the intervention deferred to after the activity rather than interrupting it
short_summary: The system detects something during an ongoing activity but withholds any response until the activity has ended, then presents its findings and the user's controls in a dedicated step.
ui_ux_rationale: Defines a non-interruptive assistance strategy and delayed review phase.
definition: The system detects something during an ongoing activity but withholds any response until the activity has ended, then presents its findings and the user's controls in a dedicated step. The activity itself runs without system intrusion. The design choice is the placement in time, and the paper argues for it explicitly against the interrupting alternative.
structural_signature: Two phases: during phase one the system observes and accumulates without emitting anything to the user; on the terminating event of phase one, phase two opens with the accumulated findings and a set of controls that act retroactively on phase-one material. Nothing the system produces is visible before the boundary, and phase-two actions can revise what phase one produced. Transplants to editing, driving, code review, form filling — anywhere an assist could have fired mid-stream.

pattern_name: interaction bounded into discrete sessions rather than running continuously
short_summary: Rather than an always-on stream, the system packages interaction into episodes with a defined opening and close.
ui_ux_rationale: Defines the opening, closing, and continuity model of the experience.
definition: Rather than an always-on stream, the system packages interaction into episodes with a defined opening and close. Each session covers a bounded slice of material and ends; the next session is a new episode rather than a continuation of the same thread. The boundary is imposed by the system, not by the user walking away.
structural_signature: Control flow is a repeated cycle with an entry condition and a terminal state: material is admitted at session start, processed through a fixed internal flow, and the session closes, after which no further turns belong to it. Session boundaries are visible as flow-diagram endpoints and as scoping for what the system may reference. Transplants to any continuous process that could have been left running — monitoring, tutoring, journaling, review.

pattern_name: suggestion summoned on demand inside the working surface
short_summary: A generated continuation is produced at the user's current position in the artifact being edited, and only when the user fires a control to ask for it.
ui_ux_rationale: Defines an inline invocation affordance and insertion point within the editor.
definition: A generated continuation is produced at the user's current position in the artifact being edited, and only when the user fires a control to ask for it. The user does not leave the editing surface to make the request or to receive the result.
structural_signature: A single user-triggered control whose output is inserted at the current insertion point of the same editable surface. There is no separate request window and no navigation step; when the control is not fired, nothing is generated, so the output's position and timing are both determined by the user's cursor and keystroke.

pattern_name: the system questions the user and the answers become the input
short_summary: The system takes the interrogative turn: it poses questions — clarification prompts, structured fields, interview turns — and the user's answers, rather than a user-composed prompt, constitute the specification the system works from.
ui_ux_rationale: Structures specification as an elicitation dialogue rather than a single prompt.
definition: The system takes the interrogative turn: it poses questions — clarification prompts, structured fields, interview turns — and the user's answers, rather than a user-composed prompt, constitute the specification the system works from. The usual prompt-then-generate direction is inverted.
structural_signature: A system-authored question precedes any user content at the head of the loop, and each reply is written into the input record consumed by the next stage. The set of questions determines which slots of the specification exist, so the user never composes a full specification unprompted.

pattern_name: extracted keywords or attributes exposed as control handles
short_summary: The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates.
ui_ux_rationale: Turns inferred concepts into editable chips, sliders, weights, or selections.
definition: The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates. The user steers subsequent behaviour by editing, weighting, selecting or deselecting members of the extracted set rather than by rewriting free text. The set is content-specific: a different input yields a different set of handles.
structural_signature: A derivation step produces a finite list of named items from the current input; those items are rendered as individually addressable widgets (chips, rows, sliders, editable fields); manipulating them re-parameterizes the downstream operation. The handle set is regenerated when the input changes, so the control panel's contents are data-dependent rather than fixed at design time.

pattern_name: demonstration or example as the specification
short_summary: Instead of describing what they want, the user supplies one or more instances of it, and the system generalizes or inverts those instances into the operative specification.
ui_ux_rationale: Lets users communicate intent by showing desired behavior or outcomes.
definition: Instead of describing what they want, the user supplies one or more instances of it, and the system generalizes or inverts those instances into the operative specification. The supplied artifact is treated as a definition of desired behaviour, not merely as content to draw on. What the system produces from it — a template, a constraint graph, a set of control states, a reusable action — is what governs subsequent generation.
structural_signature: The input slot accepts finished exemplars; an induction step converts them into a reusable structure (template, constraint set, parameter assignment, recorded macro); that structure, and not the exemplars, is what conditions later runs and what the user can edit. Adding or removing exemplars changes the induced structure.

pattern_name: generation conditioned on the user's own material
short_summary: An artifact the user already possesses or has produced — a draft, a collection, a document, a physical or staged arrangement, their own prior judgments — is ingested and used as the input the generation is conditioned on.
ui_ux_rationale: Makes existing user artifacts the contextual basis of generation.
definition: An artifact the user already possesses or has produced — a draft, a collection, a document, a physical or staged arrangement, their own prior judgments — is ingested and used as the input the generation is conditioned on. The user supplies material rather than a description of what they want. The output is a function of that material.
structural_signature: The system exposes an ingestion path for a user-owned artifact (upload, parse, encode, capture) and routes it into the generator as conditioning state, either directly or after an encoding step. The generation cannot run without that artifact; changing it changes the output. The material is pre-existing with respect to the interaction — it is not authored in order to specify the request.

pattern_name: a system or generation property exposed as a level the user sets
short_summary: A property of the system or of its output is bound to an ordered control the user sets to a value — a slider, a numbered keypress, a discrete set of levels, a spatial distance.
ui_ux_rationale: Maps a persistent system property to an ordered control.
definition: A property of the system or of its output is bound to an ordered control the user sets to a value — a slider, a numbered keypress, a discrete set of levels, a spatial distance. Setting the value re-runs or re-renders under the new setting. The dimension exists before any particular content and persists across generations.
structural_signature: A named parameter with an ordered range (short/moderate/long; 1D distance; temperature; abstraction level) is surfaced as a persistent control widget bound to that range. The control does not create content; it scales an already-defined property of whatever content is produced, and the same control is available for every output. Multiple such parameters may be exposed together as a configuration panel.

pattern_name: a fixed set of predefined prompts attached to each unit of content
short_summary: Instead of an open input box, the system attaches the same small, named menu of prepared prompts to every content unit it holds.
ui_ux_rationale: Places a predictable prompt-action menu on every content item.
definition: Instead of an open input box, the system attaches the same small, named menu of prepared prompts to every content unit it holds. Invoking one runs its prompt against that unit. The user's expressive choice is reduced to picking which of the fixed actions to apply and to which unit.
structural_signature: The content is partitioned into units; a fixed vocabulary of n named actions is defined once, system-wide; each unit exposes all n as invocable affordances, and invocation binds (action, unit) into a generation call. The action set does not vary by unit and is not editable by the user, so the interaction space is exactly units × actions. Transplants to any repository of units — a codebase with a fixed per-function action menu, a document set with a fixed per-section menu.

pattern_name: spatial arrangement on a canvas is the prompt
short_summary: The user places elements on an open two-dimensional surface and the system reads their positions and relations as specification.
ui_ux_rationale: Uses canvas position, grouping, and connection as the specification surface.
definition: The user places elements on an open two-dimensional surface and the system reads their positions and relations as specification. Proximity, grouping, and connections between elements determine what is generated, so moving an element changes the request. The canvas replaces a linear prompt field as the place where intent is expressed.
structural_signature: Elements are freely positionable on an unbounded surface; the system's input is derived from the configuration — coordinates, distances, containment, or explicit links — and not only from the elements' contents. Rearranging without changing any element's content still changes the system's output.

pattern_name: sketch or drawn stroke as the generation input
short_summary: The user's freehand mark — a stroke, a scribble, an arrow, a drawn layout — is taken as input to generation, either alongside or in place of a written prompt.
ui_ux_rationale: Uses drawn geometry as a direct input channel.
definition: The user's freehand mark — a stroke, a scribble, an arrow, a drawn layout — is taken as input to generation, either alongside or in place of a written prompt. The mark's geometry and its position carry specification, not merely selection. Each drawing pass conditions the next generated result, so drawing is the steering channel.
structural_signature: A drawing surface captures freehand vector input; the captured strokes are passed to the generator as conditioning signal; the generated result is returned into or beside the same surface so it can be drawn on again. The stroke's shape and placement are consumed as content, so two different strokes in the same location yield different results.

pattern_name: inferred or declared user state selects the system's next behavior
short_summary: The system holds a variable describing the user — mental state, intent, goal, emotion, skill level — and its current value selects among enumerated alternative behaviors: different strategies, presentation forms, or difficulty settings.
ui_ux_rationale: Adapts strategy or presentation to intent, emotion, skill, or goal.
definition: The system holds a variable describing the user — mental state, intent, goal, emotion, skill level — and its current value selects among enumerated alternative behaviors: different strategies, presentation forms, or difficulty settings. The same task content is routed through different branches depending on the value.
structural_signature: A discrete branch, lookup table, or mapping between a state variable and a fixed set of named alternative behaviors, evaluated before output is produced. The alternatives are enumerable and the mapping is authored at design time, so the behavior set is finite and the state variable is the only thing selecting among its members.

pattern_name: natural-language instruction replaces direct manipulation of the artifact
short_summary: The user states in language what they want to be true of the artifact, and the system performs the corresponding edit or retrieval.
ui_ux_rationale: Reframes interaction from procedural control to outcome-oriented conversation.
definition: The user states in language what they want to be true of the artifact, and the system performs the corresponding edit or retrieval. Language stands in for the direct-manipulation repertoire that would otherwise be used — selecting a function, adjusting a control, issuing a query. The substitution is the claim: the manipulation handles are not offered alongside.
structural_signature: The artifact has an established non-linguistic control vocabulary (transformation functions, palette editors, query forms, element handles). The interface exposes a text or utterance field as the operative control over that artifact, parses the utterance into the operation, and applies it; the user names an outcome rather than a procedure. The artifact itself remains a separate object from the language channel — the utterance is about it, not an entry in it.

pattern_name: familiar metaphor imported as the interaction surface
short_summary: The system borrows the vocabulary of an already-known artifact — a spreadsheet, a paint palette, a plant, a social feed — and uses it wholesale as the surface through which the user acts, rather than devising controls specific to the underlying operation.
ui_ux_rationale: Builds the interface from the objects and actions of a known domain.
definition: The system borrows the vocabulary of an already-known artifact — a spreadsheet, a paint palette, a plant, a social feed — and uses it wholesale as the surface through which the user acts, rather than devising controls specific to the underlying operation. The borrowed source supplies both the visual encoding and the set of legal actions.
structural_signature: The interface presents the objects of a source domain external to the system and accepts that domain's operations as its input actions; each such action is translated into a system operation, so the two sets stand in one-to-one correspondence. What is on screen is the source domain's objects and their legal actions, whether or not the paper states the mapping.

pattern_name: schema or template constrains what the model may emit
short_summary: A structure declared in advance — a schema, slot set, section skeleton, or typed taxonomy — determines the form the model's output must take.
ui_ux_rationale: Presents generated output through predefined fields, sections, or structural slots.
definition: A structure declared in advance — a schema, slot set, section skeleton, or typed taxonomy — determines the form the model's output must take. Generation is validated against or rendered into that structure rather than emitted as free text. The structure exists at the type level: it applies to every output the system produces, not just this one.
structural_signature: A named structure with enumerated parts (fields, sections, component types, category labels) is defined independently of any single generation and is stored in the system. The generator's output is emitted into, checked against, or parsed by that structure, and downstream rendering is per-part: each part gets its own visual slot, colour, or handle. Outputs that do not conform are corrected or rejected before display.

pattern_name: user-authored criteria or constraint set governing generation
short_summary: The user builds up a standing set of rules, principles, or preferences that is stored outside any single generation and consulted on every subsequent run.
ui_ux_rationale: Gives users persistent governance over future system behavior.
definition: The user builds up a standing set of rules, principles, or preferences that is stored outside any single generation and consulted on every subsequent run. Entries are authored by the user, usually in natural language, and the set is displayed as an inspectable, editable list. The set governs generation as a persistent policy rather than as a one-off instruction.
structural_signature: A named collection with add / edit / remove / reorder operations, persisted across generations and rendered as a list. Each entry originates from a user act (typed preference, feedback on an output converted into a rule, an imported written protocol) and is compiled into something the generator consults — a prompt fragment, an executable predicate, a decoding constraint, an ordering. Priority among entries may be expressed by position in the list rather than by numeric weight.

pattern_name: the system withholds the answer and hands the step back to the user
short_summary: The system runs the pipeline that would produce a terminal output but does not emit that output.
ui_ux_rationale: Preserves an essential cognitive or creative step for the person.
definition: The system runs the pipeline that would produce a terminal output but does not emit that output. What it emits instead is one step short — candidates, marked passages, correctness without the answer, questions — and the person supplies the missing final step.
structural_signature: The last stage of the pipeline is truncated at the presentation boundary: what reaches the screen is an intermediate of the process whose end product is withheld, and the interface exposes no control that reveals it. The user's action supplies the terminal value, so the loop cannot close without a human act.

pattern_name: regions the user did not mark protected from generation
short_summary: Part of the working artifact is designated off-limits and the generator is prevented from altering it, with the designation produced by the system rather than drawn by the user.
ui_ux_rationale: Establishes a preservation contract around existing user-authored material.
definition: Part of the working artifact is designated off-limits and the generator is prevented from altering it, with the designation produced by the system rather than drawn by the user. The user contributes the artifact and, implicitly, its already-authored parts; the system works out what must be preserved and enforces that during generation. Generation is thereby restricted to the complement of the protected set.
structural_signature: The artifact is partitioned into a protected subset and a mutable subset; the partition is computed (by segmentation, or by provenance of who authored each element) rather than selected; generation is then executed under a constraint or penalty that forbids modifying, overwriting or occluding the protected subset. Two things are needed and both are observable: an automatic partition step, and an enforcement mechanism at generation time. Transplants to text (generate around the user's own sentences), code (do not touch hand-written blocks), layout, audio.

pattern_name: output rendered at a fixed low fidelity with no higher-fidelity mode
short_summary: The system renders its output below the fidelity it could achieve, using a sparse representation and minimal accompanying text.
ui_ux_rationale: Uses intentionally unfinished presentation to invite user contribution.
definition: The system renders its output below the fidelity it could achieve, using a sparse representation and minimal accompanying text. The reduction is deliberate and stated as a design goal, not a technical limit. What is withheld — detail, finish, specificity — is what the user is expected to supply.
structural_signature: A ceiling is imposed on the rendering stage: outputs are emitted in a low-detail representation (outline instead of full render, one line instead of a paragraph) uniformly across all outputs, with no affordance to raise the fidelity. The invariant is that the representation underdetermines the artifact — many finished artifacts are consistent with what is shown. Transplants to wireframes instead of mockups, outlines instead of prose, thumbnails instead of masters.

pattern_name: deliberately narrowed output bandwidth to a nonvisual channel
short_summary: The system's return channel is deliberately restricted to a low-capacity, nonvisual modality, so that whatever the process produced must be compressed into a signal of very few distinguishable states.
ui_ux_rationale: Encodes system state through a deliberately limited auditory, tactile, or other signal.
definition: The system's return channel is deliberately restricted to a low-capacity, nonvisual modality, so that whatever the process produced must be compressed into a signal of very few distinguishable states. The restriction is a design commitment, not a device limitation. What can be reported back is thereby reduced to something like presence, completion, or success versus failure.
structural_signature: The output side of the loop is capped: the set of distinguishable system responses is small and finite (in the limit, binary), and is delivered on a channel with no persistent surface — the signal is transient and cannot be re-read. Consequences follow structurally: no detail can accompany the signal, and any richer state must be discarded or re-requested through some other route. Transplants to a single LED, a one-line status beep, a wristband buzz — anywhere the return path is intentionally made narrow.

pattern_name: generated candidates offered for the user to pick among
short_summary: At a single decision point the system emits more than one alternative for the same request and presents them together as a set.
ui_ux_rationale: Presents a visible choice set at a single decision point.
definition: At a single decision point the system emits more than one alternative for the same request and presents them together as a set. The user's control is exercised by choosing one member of the set rather than by editing or re-specifying. The chosen item is committed downstream and the unchosen ones are discarded or backgrounded.
structural_signature: Control flow forks at one point into N ≥ 2 outputs of the same type, all rendered simultaneously in a bounded display region (a row, a side-by-side triple, a separate list beside the working surface). A selection event on one member is the commit action: it writes that member into the downstream state and terminates the other branches. The multiplicity is in the outputs, not in the operations offered over one output, and the set is resolved in a single act.

pattern_name: two artifacts placed side by side for comparison
short_summary: Two or more instances of the same kind of artifact are displayed simultaneously in parallel regions so that their differences can be read off directly.
ui_ux_rationale: Uses aligned parallel regions to make differences directly readable.
definition: Two or more instances of the same kind of artifact are displayed simultaneously in parallel regions so that their differences can be read off directly. The layout is the mechanism: nothing is computed for the user beyond alignment and co-presence. Which instances occupy the slots may itself be user-selectable.
structural_signature: Two or more renderings of comparable objects occupy spatially parallel regions at the same time, with corresponding parts aligned across regions. The comparison quantity is the visual difference between regions, and the display may add a diff encoding over the alignment. Slot assignment is a user action ("select any two…") or a fixed before/after pairing.

pattern_name: branching or freely-ordered structure instead of a linear sequence
short_summary: The interaction is organized as a tree or open graph in which alternatives coexist, rather than as a single ordered track the user advances along.
ui_ux_rationale: Supports forking, revisiting, and switching among persistent paths.
definition: The interaction is organized as a tree or open graph in which alternatives coexist, rather than as a single ordered track the user advances along. The user can fork off a side path, pick a different branch, or take steps in an order of their choosing, and the alternatives remain live rather than being replaced. The branching structure is often itself the interface object.
structural_signature: State is held as multiple simultaneously extant paths from a shared origin; a control exists for creating a new path and for switching which path is active; paths are displayed together (as a tree, a canvas of branches, or parallel panels) so their coexistence is visible. Advancing along one path does not destroy the others.

pattern_name: one prompt fanned out to several models in parallel
short_summary: A single user request is dispatched unchanged to several distinct models at once, and their outputs are returned together.
ui_ux_rationale: Presents attributed outputs from multiple models in a shared comparison frame.
definition: A single user request is dispatched unchanged to several distinct models at once, and their outputs are returned together. The variation the user sees comes from the difference between generators rather than from sampling one generator repeatedly. The outputs are attributable to their sources and set against each other.
structural_signature: Fan-out control flow: one input, n parallel invocations differing only in which backend is called, n outputs collected and presented in a common frame with source attribution. The key structural fact is that the *generator* is the varied dimension while the input is held constant — the inverse of perturbation probing. Transplants to any plural-backend setting: several solvers, several translation engines, several search indices.

pattern_name: perturb-then-compare probing of the model
short_summary: The interface takes an input the model has already been run on, applies a controlled alteration to it, re-runs the model, and presents the altered-input output against the original one.
ui_ux_rationale: Structures exploration as a controlled counterfactual test followed by comparison.
definition: The interface takes an input the model has already been run on, applies a controlled alteration to it, re-runs the model, and presents the altered-input output against the original one. The alteration is authored or parameterized by the user, and its known content is what makes the resulting difference readable. The comparison, not either output alone, is the thing the user is given.
structural_signature: Control flow: for a held input x, the system constructs one or more variants x' by a user-specified transformation rule (granularity, target, magnitude), executes the same model on x and each x', and joins the outputs into a paired or batched display keyed to the transformation that produced each. The distinguishing structure is that the delta is *induced by the interface* rather than found in the data, so the manipulated dimension is known to the system and can be used as the organizing axis of the display. This transplants: the same signature describes a spreadsheet what-if sweep, a compiler flag sweep, or an injected-decoy audit of a retrieval index.

pattern_name: feedforward preview of a control's outcome before acting
short_summary: Each control carries, on the control itself, a rendering of what its range would produce if used.
ui_ux_rationale: Embeds representative outcomes directly into a control before commitment.
definition: Each control carries, on the control itself, a rendering of what its range would produce if used. The previews are sampled along the control's axis and are recomputed against the current state of every other control, so what is shown is the actual composed outcome, not an isolated illustration. The user therefore chooses a setting by looking rather than by trying.
structural_signature: For a control with a continuous or ordered domain, the system samples k positions in that domain, evaluates the full system output at each while holding all other controls at their present values, and renders the k results laid out along the control's own geometry. Any change to any control invalidates and re-renders every other control's samples. The two load-bearing properties are co-location of preview with control and joint conditioning across controls. Transplants to filter chains, parameter panels, configuration UIs of any kind.

pattern_name: two inputs blended or interpolated into one result
short_summary: The user selects two or more existing items and invokes an operation whose product is a single fused result rather than either operand.
ui_ux_rationale: Provides a manipulation for visibly combining source artifacts into a new output.
definition: The user selects two or more existing items and invokes an operation whose product is a single fused result rather than either operand. The blend may be continuous (interpolation along a mixing control) or discrete (a synthesized recombination). The operands remain identifiable as the things being combined, and the fusion is the system's contribution.
structural_signature: An operator takes two or more selected items as arguments and returns a result in the same space as the arguments; where the mixing is continuous, a control exposes the position between operands. Selecting the operands and invoking the operator are separate acts, and the result can itself become an operand.

pattern_name: system-filled content left editable in place
short_summary: The system pre-populates the working artifact with generated content that occupies its final position, and the user's task begins from that filled state.
ui_ux_rationale: Places generated material directly in its final editable surface.
definition: The system pre-populates the working artifact with generated content that occupies its final position, and the user's task begins from that filled state. The content is directly editable where it sits rather than being accepted or rejected as a block. The starting point is a draft, not a blank.
structural_signature: Generated material is written into the artifact's own slots before the user acts, so the artifact is non-empty at first contact. Edit affordances operate on the material in place — the same handles the user would have for their own content — and there is no separate accept step gating it into the artifact. The generated portion may be marked (highlighted as adaptable, listed as alternatives) but it is already committed.

pattern_name: segmented into discrete units, each individually addressable
short_summary: A continuous artifact is partitioned into named units, and each unit becomes an independently addressable object.
ui_ux_rationale: Gives artifact parts persistent identities and per-unit controls.
definition: A continuous artifact is partitioned into named units, and each unit becomes an independently addressable object. Operations that would otherwise apply to the whole — editing, regenerating, tagging, attributing — apply per unit. The partition is materialized on screen, and its boundaries may themselves be adjustable.
structural_signature: A single artifact is divided into a set of non-overlapping parts, each given an identity (a name, a type label, a card, a row). Each part carries its own handles, so the artifact has as many operation targets as it has parts, all simultaneously present. Segmentation may be automatic or user-adjusted, but the resulting units persist as the unit of interaction rather than dissolving back into the whole.

pattern_name: propose-critique-revise iteration loop over the same artifact
short_summary: The system opens with a concrete proposal rather than an empty field; the user reacts to it; the reaction becomes an input that yields a revised version of the same artifact.
ui_ux_rationale: Defines repeated co-creation around one persistent artifact.
definition: The system opens with a concrete proposal rather than an empty field; the user reacts to it; the reaction becomes an input that yields a revised version of the same artifact. The cycle repeats without returning to a blank specification.
structural_signature: A cycle in the control graph in which the previous output is carried into the next call together with the user's critique. Artifact identity persists across iterations — the next state is an edit of the current one, not an independent draw — so the state at round n depends on rounds 1 through n-1.

pattern_name: the operation scoped to the region or location the user marks
short_summary: The user designates a sub-extent of the artifact and the generative operation applies to exactly that extent.
ui_ux_rationale: Uses selections, masks, or spatial marks to delimit generation.
definition: The user designates a sub-extent of the artifact and the generative operation applies to exactly that extent. What lies outside the designation is not rewritten. The mark carries no content of its own: it says where, not what.
structural_signature: The artifact admits addressing of proper sub-extents (a text selection, a painted mask, a stroke set, a pane, a spatial region). A designation act records one such extent as the current scope; the operation's write set is bounded by it and the complement is held fixed; the result is composited back into the original at the marked position. The scope is re-designatable and the operation is otherwise the same regardless of which extent is chosen.

pattern_name: the model emits a program or parameterized template rather than the finished artifact
short_summary: The model's output is not the artifact the user wanted but a generator of it: code, a hierarchical program, or a parameterized template that must be executed or instantiated to yield the artifact.
ui_ux_rationale: Makes an editable generator or template the control surface for downstream artifacts.
definition: The model's output is not the artifact the user wanted but a generator of it: code, a hierarchical program, or a parameterized template that must be executed or instantiated to yield the artifact. The user's subsequent edits act on that intermediate producer, and re-running it with different arguments yields a family of artifacts. The finished object is downstream of the model's output, not identical to it.
structural_signature: Pipeline: prompt → program/template → execution → artifact. The program is a first-class, addressable object with named parts (functions, operators, parameters) and it persists after the artifact is rendered, so re-execution under different bindings is available without re-invoking the model. Diagnostic: changing an argument changes the artifact with no new generation call. Transplants to any output medium with an executable description language — layout, geometry, music, documents.

pattern_name: an existing artifact reverse-engineered into an editable representation
short_summary: A finished artifact that the system did not produce is decomposed back into an underlying structure — data table, encoding spec, component graph, layered representation — and that recovered structure becomes the object the user manipulates.
ui_ux_rationale: Exposes recovered structure such as components, layers, data, or encoding specifications.
definition: A finished artifact that the system did not produce is decomposed back into an underlying structure — data table, encoding spec, component graph, layered representation — and that recovered structure becomes the object the user manipulates. The original rendered form is treated as output whose source has been lost and must be reconstructed. Editing happens on the recovered structure, not on the surface.
structural_signature: An ingestion step takes a rendered or compiled artifact and emits a structured representation of it (typed nodes, fields, layers, specs); that representation is bound to the editing surface, and changes to it re-render the artifact. The recovery is inverse to the artifact's own production pipeline, and the representation is richer than the surface it was derived from.

pattern_name: two representations kept synchronized and editable from either side
short_summary: Two or more views of the same underlying object are shown at once, each of them editable, and an edit in any one propagates to the others.
ui_ux_rationale: Provides bidirectional editing across multiple views of the same object.
definition: Two or more views of the same underlying object are shown at once, each of them editable, and an edit in any one propagates to the others. Neither view is subordinate: the user may work in whichever is convenient and the system reconciles them. The conversion runs in both directions rather than compiling one representation into the other.
structural_signature: A shared model backs multiple concurrently displayed representations; each representation has write access to the model; a propagation step updates the sibling representations after any write. The loop is closed — starting in representation A, converting to B, and editing B returns a valid state in A.

pattern_name: manual authoring path retained beside the generated one
short_summary: Alongside the generative route, the interface keeps a route by which the user authors the same material directly: a free-text field, editable nodes, a custom operation, a user-added prompt.
ui_ux_rationale: Preserves choice between direct creation and AI assistance throughout the task.
definition: Alongside the generative route, the interface keeps a route by which the user authors the same material directly: a free-text field, editable nodes, a custom operation, a user-added prompt. Neither route is a fallback mode; both are available at the same time.
structural_signature: Two input routes converge on the same artifact slot — one generated, one hand-authored — with no mode switch between them, and the artifact can record contributions from both. Removing the generator leaves the interface still operable for that slot; the slot's schema is identical whichever route filled it.

pattern_name: fixed disposition set offered on every suggestion
short_summary: Every system-produced item arrives with the same small, closed set of actions attached to it, so the user's response to any suggestion is drawn from a uniform vocabulary.
ui_ux_rationale: Attaches consistent controls such as accept, edit, regenerate, insert, or ignore to each item.
definition: Every system-produced item arrives with the same small, closed set of actions attached to it, so the user's response to any suggestion is drawn from a uniform vocabulary. The unit of disposition is the individual item, not the batch. The specific set varies by system — accept/regenerate/edit, replace/abstract, insert/ignore — but its fixity and its per-item attachment are what the pattern names.
structural_signature: Each generated item is rendered with a co-located control group whose members are identical across items and constant across the session; activating a member commits a disposition for that item alone and leaves other items untouched. The set is enumerable and closed, and there is no path for disposing of items that is not in the set.

pattern_name: the run can be suspended, redirected or exited mid-flight
short_summary: A process that would otherwise run to completion is made interruptible: the user can halt it, change its parameters while it continues, or leave it before it ends.
ui_ux_rationale: Gives users ongoing agency over a non-atomic process.
definition: A process that would otherwise run to completion is made interruptible: the user can halt it, change its parameters while it continues, or leave it before it ends. The intervention lands during execution, not before it starts or after it returns. The unit of generation or simulation is thereby made non-atomic.
structural_signature: The executing process exposes a control channel that remains live while it runs; commands on that channel (pause, substitute a parameter, resume, abort) take effect on the in-flight run rather than queueing for the next one. The system therefore holds partial state that is valid to inspect and to modify mid-execution.

pattern_name: explicit control structure over dialogue turns
short_summary: The sequence of conversational turns is governed by an authored control structure — a finite state machine, a protocol tree, a fixed phase sequence, a structured prompting scheme — rather than by the model's turn-by-turn discretion.
ui_ux_rationale: Defines allowable conversational states and transitions.
definition: The sequence of conversational turns is governed by an authored control structure — a finite state machine, a protocol tree, a fixed phase sequence, a structured prompting scheme — rather than by the model's turn-by-turn discretion. The structure is a designed object, sometimes authorable by non-programmers.
structural_signature: A graph or ordered stage list exists as an inspectable (often editable) object: nodes carry what the agent says or does, edges carry conditions evaluated on the interlocutor's response. The current node is persistent state, and a transition is computed at every turn, so the reachable next turns are a function of position in the structure.

pattern_name: fixed staged pipeline the user is walked through
short_summary: Work advances through an ordered series of stages that is fixed by the designer before the user arrives.
ui_ux_rationale: Organizes work as a stable designer-authored sequence.
definition: Work advances through an ordered series of stages that is fixed by the designer before the user arrives. The interface makes the ordering visible and moves the user along it, one stage at a time. Iteration within a stage or between neighbouring stages may be permitted, but the sequence itself is not authored by the user.
structural_signature: A stage list S1…Sn exists in the system independent of any particular input, and each stage has its own module, section, or screen. The surface encodes the order (sections laid out in workflow order, a guided sequence of overlays, a chain of modules each consuming the previous one's output), and advancement is by completing or passing a stage rather than by free navigation. The number and identity of stages are constant across runs.

pattern_name: the task decomposed into parts handled one at a time
short_summary: A goal supplied at runtime is broken into smaller sub-parts, and the parts are produced or handled serially rather than in one shot.
ui_ux_rationale: Turns a runtime goal into inspectable, sequential sub-tasks.
definition: A goal supplied at runtime is broken into smaller sub-parts, and the parts are produced or handled serially rather than in one shot. The decomposition is derived from the particular goal, so its shape varies with the input. Each part surfaces as its own step that can be inspected or edited before the next is taken.
structural_signature: An input goal is transformed into an ordered list of sub-parts whose length and identity are computed per input (by the system, the user, or both). Each sub-part is executed or generated separately, in sequence, and appears as a discrete step in the interface; the final artifact is assembled from the parts. The sequence exists only for this goal — a different goal yields a different sequence.

pattern_name: revisitable history, versioning and replay
short_summary: Prior states and actions are retained as first-class records rather than discarded when superseded.
ui_ux_rationale: Makes prior states available for restoration, continuation, branching, or playback.
definition: Prior states and actions are retained as first-class records rather than discarded when superseded. The interface exposes them as a navigable set the user can return to, resume from, or play back in time order. History is an object in the system, not just a side effect of use.
structural_signature: Every state change appends an addressable record (a version, a modification entry, an accept/reject/edit event, a timestamped frame). The interface renders the record set as a navigable structure — a list, a stream, a timeline — and supports two operations over it: returning to a past state and continuing from there, and traversing the sequence in temporal order. Records survive the session and the same view may serve live and retrospective inspection.

pattern_name: linked views where selecting one element highlights its counterpart
short_summary: Two or more display regions show the same underlying items under different encodings, and a correspondence between them is maintained and made visible.
ui_ux_rationale: Coordinates multiple representations through visible correspondence.
definition: Two or more display regions show the same underlying items under different encodings, and a correspondence between them is maintained and made visible. Acting on an element in one region changes the rendering of its counterpart in the others. The correspondence is the interface's claim: nothing shown in one view is orphaned from its counterpart elsewhere.
structural_signature: A set of items has more than one simultaneous rendering, and the system holds an identity mapping between renderings. A selection, brush, or hover event in region A triggers a rendering change (highlight, filter, scroll, annotation) on the mapped elements in region B, with the mapping stable across interactions. As clustered, the category also contains members where the correspondence is a fixed link from an output element to its source span rather than an interactive coordination — see the review flag.

pattern_name: inspectable intermediate representation between input and output
short_summary: The pipeline from input to output passes through a named intermediate artifact that is rendered for the user to read.
ui_ux_rationale: Renders an intermediate artifact for reading or editing before final output.
definition: The pipeline from input to output passes through a named intermediate artifact that is rendered for the user to read. That intermediate — a sentence, a block of code, a set of extracted entities, a prompt — is the object the user inspects and often edits, and the final output is produced from it. The mediation is deliberate: the system refuses to map input straight to output.
structural_signature: Between the user's input and the delivered artifact sits at least one representation that is (a) materialized as a distinct object in the system, (b) displayed in a human-readable form, and (c) actually consumed by the next stage to produce the output. Editing or rejecting the intermediate changes the output; the output cannot be produced without passing through it. Some members of this cluster are load-bearing on inspectability alone (the human reads the intermediate and makes the decision) rather than on editability.

pattern_name: the model's interpretation of the input externalized on screen
short_summary: The system displays its own reading of what the user supplied — the construal, the inferred intent, the context it thinks it is in — as a first-class object rather than only acting on it.
ui_ux_rationale: Makes inferred intent or context visible and potentially correctable.
definition: The system displays its own reading of what the user supplied — the construal, the inferred intent, the context it thinks it is in — as a first-class object rather than only acting on it. The user can therefore see where the system's understanding diverges from their own, and in several cases can edit that understanding directly. The displayed object stands between the user's input and whatever the system produces next.
structural_signature: An inference step over the user's input emits a named artifact (graph, keyword overlay, natural-language restatement, schema instance) that is rendered persistently on screen; downstream behaviour is conditioned on that artifact. Where the artifact is editable, edits to it — not to the original input — are the channel by which the user corrects the system.

pattern_name: the agent's plan rendered on screen before execution
short_summary: Before acting, the system displays the sequence of actions it intends to take, and that display persists as the actions are carried out.
ui_ux_rationale: Presents intended actions as a persistent plan, diagram, or step list.
definition: Before acting, the system displays the sequence of actions it intends to take, and that display persists as the actions are carried out. The plan is a visible object with its own structure — a diagram, a step list, a lookahead lane — and in several systems it is editable, so the user can alter the plan rather than react to its results. Commitment status may be encoded so the user can tell which parts are still revisable.
structural_signature: A planning step emits an ordered structure of forthcoming operations that is rendered before any of them executes; execution then advances through that structure while it remains on screen. Where the structure is editable, edits to unexecuted elements change what will run; visual encoding distinguishes executed, committed, and still-provisional elements.

pattern_name: pre-send inspection of what is about to leave
short_summary: A checkpoint is interposed between composing content and transmitting it, at which the outgoing payload is displayed to the user together with the system's assessment of it.
ui_ux_rationale: Inserts a deliberate review and correction checkpoint before transmission.
definition: A checkpoint is interposed between composing content and transmitting it, at which the outgoing payload is displayed to the user together with the system's assessment of it. The user can edit, redact, or abstract before the content crosses the boundary. The design commitment is that the intervention is visible and happens on the user's side of the transmission.
structural_signature: Transmission is gated by a review state in which the exact payload is rendered, annotated with system-computed marks or scores, and made editable; the send proceeds only from that state, and edits made there change what is transmitted. The processing that produces the annotation runs before the boundary crossing, so the gate is client-side with respect to the recipient.

pattern_name: drill-down from aggregate overview to individual instance
short_summary: The same collection is presented at more than one level of granularity, from an aggregate summary down to a single item.
ui_ux_rationale: Provides navigation across levels of granularity.
definition: The same collection is presented at more than one level of granularity, from an aggregate summary down to a single item. Interaction at a coarser level selects the population shown at the finer level. The finest level exposes the individual case behind the aggregate.
structural_signature: A hierarchy of at least two views over one collection, ordered by an aggregation relation: the coarse view displays a function of many items, the fine view displays items themselves. A selection in the coarse view is a filter that defines the fine view's contents, and the levels are simultaneously present or one-click reachable. The ordering is asymmetric — the fine level cannot substitute for the coarse one.

pattern_name: corpus laid out as a spatial map as the browse surface
short_summary: A large collection of items is projected into a two-dimensional layout, and that layout — not a list, not a feed — is the primary surface the user navigates.
ui_ux_rationale: Uses a two-dimensional similarity layout as the primary exploration interface.
definition: A large collection of items is projected into a two-dimensional layout, and that layout — not a list, not a feed — is the primary surface the user navigates. Position encodes relatedness computed by the system, so proximity is meaningful. Queries and selections act on the map by re-weighting or re-highlighting it rather than by returning a separate result list.
structural_signature: A layout algorithm assigns each item a position in a shared 2-D space from a computed similarity or relation structure; the resulting arrangement is rendered as a pannable/zoomable canvas that is the main navigation control. Interaction operates on positions and neighbourhoods, and any query result is expressed as a change to the map's state rather than as a new view.

pattern_name: model internals rendered as an inspectable view
short_summary: Quantities from inside the computation — attention weights, token or answer ranks, per-head importance, the spans the model relied on — are surfaced as a view the user can read and manipulate.
ui_ux_rationale: Visualizes attention, rankings, relied-upon spans, or other computational quantities.
definition: Quantities from inside the computation — attention weights, token or answer ranks, per-head importance, the spans the model relied on — are surfaced as a view the user can read and manipulate. What is displayed is not the output but the machinery that produced it. The view supports operations over those quantities, such as ranking, pruning, or comparing them.
structural_signature: The display is bound to intermediate values captured during inference rather than to the emitted result; those values are aggregated or projected into a view with its own controls (metric selectors, per-unit comparison, ablation toggles). Changing a control re-derives the view from the same captured values without re-running the user's task.

pattern_name: disclosure of how the output was produced
short_summary: Alongside an output, the system displays information about how that output came about: the derivation of a score, a confidence value, an uncertainty estimate, a quality diagnosis, or the agent's own stated reasoning.
ui_ux_rationale: Places provenance, confidence, uncertainty, or reasoning beside an output.
definition: Alongside an output, the system displays information about how that output came about: the derivation of a score, a confidence value, an uncertainty estimate, a quality diagnosis, or the agent's own stated reasoning. The disclosure adds no new task content.
structural_signature: A secondary display element bound one-to-one to a primary output element, carrying process metadata rather than task content. Its content is produced by or read from the producing pipeline, not from the user's material; removing it leaves the output intact and the task still performable.

pattern_name: a per-unit attribute encoded by colour or typography in the content itself
short_summary: Every unit of displayed content — a word, line, span, or segment — carries a value on some attribute, and that value is rendered by altering the appearance of the unit in place: colour, opacity, weight.
ui_ux_rationale: Uses styling to encode values directly on content units.
definition: Every unit of displayed content — a word, line, span, or segment — carries a value on some attribute, and that value is rendered by altering the appearance of the unit in place: colour, opacity, weight. The attribute is read off the content itself rather than from a separate annotation layer or panel.
structural_signature: A one-to-one map from content units to attribute values, rendered as a visual variable of each unit; the content's text, order, and layout are unchanged, so stripping the encoding restores the original artifact exactly. The display allocates no separate region to the attribute, and the number of encoded marks equals the number of content units.

pattern_name: flagged spans highlighted in place with detail revealed on demand
short_summary: The system marks particular locations inside the user's content and attaches a deeper layer of material to each mark that is not shown until the user asks for it.
ui_ux_rationale: Combines lightweight inline indicators with expandable detail.
definition: The system marks particular locations inside the user's content and attaches a deeper layer of material to each mark that is not shown until the user asks for it. The first layer is a lightweight in-content indicator; the second is an expandable panel, popup, or tab bar holding explanation, alternatives, or scores. Detail is thus staged rather than presented all at once.
structural_signature: Per-unit annotations are rendered inline at their source location; each annotation is an interactive trigger (hover, click, expand) that opens a secondary container holding additional per-unit material. Collapsing the container returns the display to the marked-but-undetailed state, so the content view never carries the full detail at rest.

pattern_name: the model's judgment placed alongside the person's own
short_summary: The interface puts the system's assessment next to the user's own assessment of the same thing, so the two can be read against each other.
ui_ux_rationale: Structures reflection by having users compare committed human and AI assessments.
definition: The interface puts the system's assessment next to the user's own assessment of the same thing, so the two can be read against each other. Typically the user commits to a position first and the model's position is then revealed, with a further step in which the user may revise. The juxtaposition, and the divergence it exposes, is the designed object.
structural_signature: Two verdicts over the same item are held in the interface — one produced by the user, one by the system — and are displayed in the same view or in a fixed temporal order (user commits, system reveals, user re-decides). A revision affordance follows the reveal, and the difference between the two verdicts is itself rendered or computed.

pattern_name: a single aggregate score as the summary readout
short_summary: Many underlying events or measurements are collapsed into one number on a fixed scale, and that number is the interface's headline element.
ui_ux_rationale: Compresses underlying evidence into a bounded headline value.
definition: Many underlying events or measurements are collapsed into one number on a fixed scale, and that number is the interface's headline element. The score stands in for the history that produced it; the individual contributions are not the readout. Its bounded range gives the user a position rather than a raw quantity.
structural_signature: An accumulator over a stream of events is displayed as one scalar on a declared bounded interval, occupying a persistent, prominent slot in the layout. Structurally: many-to-one reduction, fixed range, single display element, updated as events arrive. No per-event breakdown is required for the pattern to hold, and the reduction function is the system's, not the user's. Transplants to any domain that scores a stream — a credit-style rating, a code-health number, a fitness ring.

pattern_name: persona or stance assigned to the agent
short_summary: A character specification — a name, personality, social role, or narrative voice — is attached to the generative agent and held constant across its turns.
ui_ux_rationale: Establishes a persistent social role, voice, or perspective for the AI.
definition: A character specification — a name, personality, social role, or narrative voice — is attached to the generative agent and held constant across its turns. It is treated as a design element that can be set, swapped, or compared, independent of the task the agent performs.
structural_signature: A persistent specification slot, separate from turn-level content, is applied to every generated turn. Changing only that slot changes the voice and role of all subsequent output while task, inputs, and every other interface element stay fixed; the slot is a controlled variable of the system, not a property of any one response.

pattern_name: a generated scenario the user enters as a participant
short_summary: The system generates a bounded scenario and places the user inside it as a participant rather than as an operator addressing a tool.
ui_ux_rationale: Frames interaction as role-play inside a bounded situation rather than tool operation.
definition: The system generates a bounded scenario and places the user inside it as a participant rather than as an operator addressing a tool. The user acts in role, and the model plays the other parties or the environment; the run can be repeated. What the user produces during the run is behaviour in the scenario, not a request to the model.
structural_signature: Control flow: a setup step fixes the scenario's parameters (topic, role, self-representation), after which the interface switches into an in-scenario mode where the user's turns are read as actions of a participant and the model's turns are read as the world's response. The scenario has an entry and an exit, and re-entry restarts it rather than continuing it. The signature is the *frame switch* — user input stops being instructions to a system and becomes conduct inside a generated world. Transplants to sales rehearsal, incident drills, or a generated market a strategy is tested against.

pattern_name: several co-present participants around one system
short_summary: More than one party is present at the same system instance at the same time — two humans, a dyad, a group, or humans plus a population of agents — and the design allocates distinct roles among them.
ui_ux_rationale: Organizes a shared experience for multiple humans, agents, or mixed groups.
definition: More than one party is present at the same system instance at the same time — two humans, a dyad, a group, or humans plus a population of agents — and the design allocates distinct roles among them. The system is addressed to the configuration rather than to a single user.
structural_signature: At least two simultaneous role slots on one system instance, each with its own input rights, and system behavior that depends on which role acted. Removing one participant leaves the interaction structurally incomplete — a role goes unfilled — rather than merely reducing the number of users.

pattern_name: role-asymmetric surfaces over one system
short_summary: One system presents deliberately different surfaces to different classes of participant, so what each party can see and do depends on their role.
ui_ux_rationale: Gives participant classes different views, information, controls, or communication channels over shared state.
definition: One system presents deliberately different surfaces to different classes of participant, so what each party can see and do depends on their role. The asymmetry is designed rather than incidental: some information is withheld from one side, or an extra channel exists for the other. The parties nonetheless act on a shared underlying state.
structural_signature: A single backend serves two or more role-specific front-ends or channels whose contents differ by construction; a role assignment determines which view a session receives; at least one channel is private to one role. State written by any role is visible to the others only through their own role's view.

pattern_name: the model fills all but one role of a multi-party procedure
short_summary: A procedure defined over two or more roles is run by one person alone, with the model filling every role but theirs.
ui_ux_rationale: Converts a coordinated group activity into a single-user experience supported by AI roles.
definition: A procedure defined over two or more roles is run by one person alone, with the model filling every role but theirs. The scheduling and co-presence requirements disappear; the activity becomes asynchronous and single-user. The interaction retains the shape of the multi-party original.
structural_signature: The system takes a procedure defined over n≥2 human participants and reassigns all roles but one to the model, leaving a single-user loop that runs at the remaining participant's own pace. Structurally: role count unchanged, human count reduced to one, synchronization constraint removed. Observable in the paper as a mapping from the multi-party procedure's roles onto the agent's behaviours. Transplants to pair programming, moderated review, negotiation practice, peer critique.

pattern_name: the system's participants presented as one kind of entity while composed of another
short_summary: The system presents itself to its users as one kind of thing while operating as another, and the discrepancy is a designed property rather than an omission.
ui_ux_rationale: Designs the experience around perceived identity, concealment, and eventual reveal.
definition: The system presents itself to its users as one kind of thing while operating as another, and the discrepancy is a designed property rather than an omission. The concealment is held for a defined period, and the moment of revealing is itself scheduled into the control flow. Users' interpretations before and after the reveal are both part of the design.
structural_signature: Two descriptions of the system co-exist: the description presented in the interface, and the actual composition of the entities behind it. Only the first is available to users while the system runs. The signature is the mismatch between the two, and it is independent of what is being concealed. Transplants to any system with participants whose nature can be misdescribed — a marketplace, a review site, a game lobby.

pattern_name: the artifact under construction embodied as the interlocutor
short_summary: The object the user is authoring is instantiated as a conversational agent, and the user develops it by talking to it in character rather than by editing a representation of it.
ui_ux_rationale: Collapses editing and testing into conversation with the artifact itself.
definition: The object the user is authoring is instantiated as a conversational agent, and the user develops it by talking to it in character rather than by editing a representation of it. Answers the agent gives become part of the object's specification. Editing and testing collapse into the same act.
structural_signature: The work object's current specification is bound to an agent's conditioning; the user's only interaction surface with that object is dialogue with the agent so conditioned; the agent's replies are treated as further content of the object, feeding back into the specification. Structurally: the artifact's state and the interlocutor's state are the same state, and there is no separate editable rendering of the object. Transplants wherever an artifact can be voiced — a product spec interviewed as a "customer", a policy queried as itself.

pattern_name: successive workflow stages sharing state in a single environment
short_summary: Task stages that were previously carried out in distinct tools, windows, or databases are placed inside one environment where they share state.
ui_ux_rationale: Consolidates previously separate tools or windows into one state-sharing workspace.
definition: Task stages that were previously carried out in distinct tools, windows, or databases are placed inside one environment where they share state. The consolidation itself, rather than any individual stage, is what the design claims.
structural_signature: One application shell containing two or more stages of a workflow whose state is shared, such that the output of one stage is directly addressable in another with no export/import step. Only half of this is observable in the artifact — several stage regions plus shared state; the "previously separate" half is a claim about prior tooling, and cannot be read off the interface.

pattern_name: open dialogue running alongside the artifact being viewed
short_summary: A free-form conversational channel is live at the same time as a non-conversational artifact the user is attending to, and the turns are about that artifact.
ui_ux_rationale: Keeps an artifact and a conversation about it simultaneously available.
definition: A free-form conversational channel is live at the same time as a non-conversational artifact the user is attending to, and the turns are about that artifact. The artifact persists on display; the dialogue neither replaces it nor is required to advance it.
structural_signature: Two concurrently live regions (possibly on two devices): one holds a persistent artifact that is not consumed by the exchange, the other accepts an unbounded number of user-authored natural-language turns scoped to that artifact. Removing the dialogue channel leaves the artifact usable; removing the artifact leaves the dialogue without a referent.

pattern_name: workspace partitioned into fixed functional panels
short_summary: The screen is divided into a fixed number of persistent regions, each with an assigned function that does not change during use.
ui_ux_rationale: Assigns stable roles to persistent workspace regions.
definition: The screen is divided into a fixed number of persistent regions, each with an assigned function that does not change during use. The partition is stated as a design decision: which functions get their own region, and where each sits. Regions may differ in what they permit, for instance which of them accepts typing.
structural_signature: A stable spatial decomposition of one workspace into n named regions, each bound to a function (input, corpus, codebook, canvas, generated output, controls). Region identity and position persist across the session; content changes inside a region but its role does not. Spatial arrangement may encode something further — process order, or an editability asymmetry between regions.

pattern_name: two alternative presentation modes for the same content
short_summary: The same content is made available under two different presentation or interaction disciplines, and a selection determines which is in force.
ui_ux_rationale: Provides switchable interaction disciplines over one content payload.
definition: The same content is made available under two different presentation or interaction disciplines, and a selection determines which is in force. The modes differ in how the content is reached and acted on, not in what the content is. Only one mode operates at a time.
structural_signature: One content payload, two renderings with distinct interaction rules (push stream vs. pull query; predetermined navigation vs. free-form questioning; freeform text vs. structured fields; whole-document vs. extracted-terms conditioning), and a mode selector that makes one active. The modes are alternatives at the same point in the flow — either can serve the same user need — and switching between them does not change the underlying content. In several members the two modes are never both available to the same user; there the selector is the experimenter's assignment rather than a control (see the review flag).

pattern_name: assistance grafted into an existing tool, page or workflow
short_summary: The generative capability is attached to a host artifact that the system did not author — a third-party application, a web page, a chat client, an established workflow.
ui_ux_rationale: Anchors AI functions to identifiable locations in a host surface.
definition: The generative capability is attached to a host artifact that the system did not author — a third-party application, a web page, a chat client, an established workflow. The host keeps its own structure and remains usable without the addition. The design move is the attachment point: where in the host the capability is inserted.
structural_signature: Two separable layers exist: a pre-existing host surface with its own controls and content, and an added layer (plugin, browser extension overlay, injected step, docked component) that renders generated content into or beside the host. The added layer is anchored to identifiable host locations — particular spans of host content, particular stages of the host's flow, particular composition steps — and the anchoring, not the generation, is what the paper specifies. Detaching the layer leaves the host intact.

pattern_name: scrollable chat-log surface with a text-entry area
short_summary: The interaction surface is a vertically scrolling transcript of alternating turns with a persistent composition area anchored below it.
ui_ux_rationale: Uses an append-only transcript above a persistent composition region.
definition: The interaction surface is a vertically scrolling transcript of alternating turns with a persistent composition area anchored below it. The transcript is the record and the display at once: earlier turns remain addressable by scrolling, and new turns append to the end. Nothing about the layout is specialized to the task; the same surface would serve any turn-taking exchange.
structural_signature: Two regions: an append-only scrollable list of turn elements attributed to a speaker, and a fixed input region containing a text field plus a send affordance. New content enters at one end; the viewport auto-follows or can be scrolled back; history persists in the same region it was produced in. This is fully statable without reference to what the turns are about, which is precisely why it recurs across unrelated domains.

pattern_name: the agent's presence and actions shown inside the shared artifact
short_summary: The system's activity is rendered within the work surface itself — as cursors, marks, live strokes, or attached companions — instead of being confined to a separate conversation panel.
ui_ux_rationale: Renders agent cursors, marks, strokes, or companions in the artifact's coordinate space.
definition: The system's activity is rendered within the work surface itself — as cursors, marks, live strokes, or attached companions — instead of being confined to a separate conversation panel. The user sees where the agent is and what it is touching while they continue to work in the same space. Presence cues are persistent and positioned relative to the artifact's content.
structural_signature: Agent state is drawn in the same coordinate space as the user's content, anchored to specific locations or to the pointer, and updates while the user is acting rather than only between turns. There is no separate container that owns the agent; removing the artifact view would remove the agent's visible form.

pattern_name: embodied character or avatar as the agent's form
short_summary: The agent is given a rendered body — an animated character, a 3-D figure, an on-screen avatar, a participant tile — and the user addresses that figure rather than a text pane.
ui_ux_rationale: Gives the agent a visible body, character, expression, or participant tile.
definition: The agent is given a rendered body — an animated character, a 3-D figure, an on-screen avatar, a participant tile — and the user addresses that figure rather than a text pane. The body is the locus of the agent's turns: speech, expression, or animation issue from it. Several papers treat embodiment as a graded design variable with the text pane as the low end.
structural_signature: A persistent visual figure with its own extent and position is rendered in the interface, and the system's outputs are attributed to and emitted from that figure rather than from an undifferentiated output region. The figure occupies a slot ordinarily held by a human participant (a tile, a seat, a character in a scene).

pattern_name: output spatially registered to the physical scene
short_summary: Generated content is placed in the coordinate frame of a real scene, or of captured video of one, and attached to a referent within it rather than to a panel.
ui_ux_rationale: Anchors generated content to real-world referents.
definition: Generated content is placed in the coordinate frame of a real scene, or of captured video of one, and attached to a referent within it rather than to a panel. When the referent moves, the output moves with it.
